note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Nov 12 NY close: Oct Treasury deficit $404B — a record for the month, +42% y/y (receipts $369B, outlays a record $773B); FY2026 deficit $1.992T, 6.2% of GDP; the $25B 30Y auction tailed 0.4bp (5.441%, BTC 2.36).
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: Nov 13 Asia: no new growth prints overnight — US PPI (7:30am CT) and EZ GDP 2nd est. (4:00am CT) are the day's tests; claims missed Thu (200K vs 194K). Nov 12 NY close: claims miss 200K vs 194K; existing-home sales -5.5% to 3.75M SAAR, lowest since Aug 2010 (30Y mortgage averaged 7.33% in Oct); UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q in line, Q2 revised to a -1.0% contraction. US PPI Fri 7:30am CT (+0.4% m/m fcst); EZ GDP (2nd est.) Fri 4:00am CT.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Nov 13 Asia: PPI Fri 7:30am CT (+0.4% m/m, core +0.3% fcst; +6.6%/+5.0% y/y expected) closes the inflation week after the hot CPI (+0.4%/core +0.3%). Nov 12 NY close: the CPI print digests (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%, third straight +0.3% core); US PPI Fri 7:30am CT (+0.4% m/m, core +0.3% fcst) closes the inflation week; Japan PPI beat +7.1% y/y (fcst 6.5%).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Nov 13 Asia: DXY ~103.15 holds the 19-month high; Dec Fed hike effectively certain — 25bp ~85-86%, 50bp tail ~14.5% (CME FedWatch via FXStreet); Williams Thu: 'still has work to do', inflation 'too high'. 2Y ~4.86% (+34bp in two sessions), 10Y ~5.11%. Nov 12 NY open: claims miss (200K vs 194K) leaves Dec Fed pricing unmoved at ~91% 25bp (CME) / ~88% (LSEG). Nov 12 NY open: Dec Fed hike 25bp ~91% (CME FedWatch), 50bp tail ~9-13%; BoE Dec back-to-back ~75% (Reuters); BoJ Dec ~84% intact despite Asada pushback. Williams panel late Thu. Nov 12 Asia: DXY 103.02 — a 19-month high; Dec Fed hike ~87% 25bp / ~13% 50bp (unchanged overnight); Deutsche Bank now sees three hikes (Dec, Jan, Mar), UBS two (Dec, Mar), Goldman another early next year. Williams speaks late Thu. Nov 11 London: DXY to a four-week high (~102.5) as the Dec Fed hike firms — FedWatch 25bp ~85% (Reuters 09:15Z) after 91.9% in Asia, 50bp tail ~9-15%; the hike itself essentially certain. Paulson: CPI “shows that inflationary pressures remain clearly evident”; Logan: “at least two more rate increases, each by 25bp”. Nov 11 NY close: DXY 102.86 (+0.64%), highest since April 2025; Dec Fed hike 25bp ~87% (CME FedWatch via Reuters), 50bp tail ~13%; ECB ~92%, BoJ ~84%, BoE back-to-back ~67% (morning briefing pricing). Nov 12 NY close: DXY 103.16 (+0.3%), a 19-month high; Dec Fed hike 25bp ~91% (CME FedWatch), 50bp tail ~9-12%; Goolsbee: inflation 'well-above target', 'sober minded' on pace; ECB ~88%, BoJ ~84% (STIR 21bp), BoE back-to-back ~70-75% (STIR 69%).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Nov 10: next CFTC cut (Nov 10 positions) due Fri Nov 13 — Veterans Day Wed may shift the release; the Nov 3 cut (released Nov 6) is still the latest scored. Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4. Next CFTC release Fri Nov 6, 2:30pm CT — the 4pm run picks it up. Nov 3 CFTC cut released Fri 2:30pm CT — percentile scoring vs the Oct 27 cut carries to the 2am run; board scores unchanged. Nov 3 CFTC (released Nov 6): EUR net short -157,791 (5th pct of 20y, 11-yr extreme) and JPY net long +102,321 (98th pct) still crowded; GBP's short unwound (+19,593 w/w to -59,821) out of the extreme — GBP positioning score 1 → 0. AUD -129,457 and NZD -60,015 still crowded short; CAD -41,775 after heavy covering (+24,649). Next CFTC cut (Nov 10 data) due later this week.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Nov 13 Asia: DXY holds the 19-month high (~103.15) in consolidation; equities steady after Thu's mixed tape (S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq flat; NVDA -5.8% on the CEO resignation). Nov 12 NY close: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns — NVDA -5.8% midday, AMD +5.6% on an upgrade; S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq flat; VIX ~18.3 (early snapshot, up from 17.49 Wed close); gold -2.8% as the 10Y tops 5.10%.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Nov 13 Asia: Brent ~$95.73 / WTI ~$88.28 after Thu's +$3.06/+2.6% settle jump on Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites (East-West pipeline, Yanbu, Aramco Riyadh); gold ~$3,875 after Thu's -2.8% slide. Nov 12 NY close: Brent $93.47 / WTI $86.49 (futures settlements) — EIA crude +4.657M vs a -1.109M draw expected, smaller than API's +9.0M so taken as relief; gold ~$3,874 (-2.8%), below $3,900 as real yields rise.
